title: Fresh-seed review (12) of c41's CIPS propulsion negative: replicated; chi 6 and chi 4.5 nucleate 41 and 30 bodies that freeze into a static lattice with 0 splits and at most 2.0-2.3 labkit body lengths, while the default chi 3 on the same seed nucleates 7 and divides (7 persistent splits, generation 2)
summary: Ran the finding's world.py unchanged on seed 12 (labkit, 192^2, 100 frames, t=10000) at chi 6, chi 4.5 and the default chi 3. chi 6: 41 nucleations, 40 round bodies at the end in a static lattice (chi6/seed12/sheet.png from t=900 on), 0 splits, max speed 0.0020, max 2.0 labkit body lengths. chi 4.5: 30 nucleations, 0 splits, max speed 0.0026, max 2.3 body lengths. Default: 7 nucleations, 8 splits (7 persistent, generation 2), 15 bodies at the end, max 1.2 body lengths. Stronger drift up the product turns sparse growing dividers into a dense static lattice and gives no self-propelled condensate, as the finding says.

observations.M: negative replicated: chi6/seed12 and chi45/seed12 FACTS.md, 0 persistent splits, max 2.0 and 2.3 labkit body lengths, static lattice in chi6/seed12/sheet.png; control default/seed12: 7 nucleations, 7 persistent splits

seeds_run.result: replicates: chi 6 41 bodies / 0 splits, chi 4.5 30 / 0, default 7 nucleations / 7 persistent splits

verdicts.limitation: Two of the eight arms (chi 6, chi 4.5) on one fresh seed; Dp 0.3 and raised turnover not re-run. labkit's body lengths use sqrt(area) for round bodies, the right unit here.
